## The fork, put to the maintainer

Item 1 is a security-boundary choice, so it goes to Warren rather than being picked here. What the reading found:

- The runtime gate is a pure name match (`missingCapabilities`, `@objectstack/core`): a `requiredPermissions` gate admits a caller whose sets' `systemPermissions` name the token, declared or not.
- What a `capability` declaration adds: its Setup label, `scope: 'org'` (condition (c) of the organization-admin boundary, ADR-0090 D12), and the exemption that lets a set granting the app's own token bind to `everyone` (ADR-0090 D5 revision, `describeHighPrivilegeBits`). Dropping declarations from a copy loses all three.
- The registry entry's reason for code-only is "nothing in code would ever require the name". Environment-authored actions, flows and objects now carry `requiredPermissions`, and an unmanaged copy is exactly environment metadata that both requires and grants the token.

Recommended (building on it while the ruling is pending): `capability` becomes runtime-creatable (overlay stays closed, so a packaged declaration cannot be re-scoped); an environment save under a platform capability name or a name a package holds is refused; the unmanaged import copies capabilities and, under `targetNamespace`, renames `<ns>.` / `<ns>_` capability names and rewrites `systemPermissions` / `requiredPermissions`. Alternative: keep code-only and have templates declare no `capabilities[]` (gating still works; label, org scope and `everyone` binding are lost).

Item 2: the scaffold stops writing connector plugins into a project that declares no connector (the README says how to add one with its connector). The install contract is unchanged.

coordinator#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbXuXMUwP5Bbmq6UZRJ

**Ruled: option A** — a capability is runtime-creatable, platform names and package-held names are refused at the save door, and an unmanaged copy copies an app's capabilities, renamed with the copy when it takes a new namespace.

Maintainer, verbatim, in the project thread at 2026-11-19T04:31Z: 「同意」. It answers the seat's business explanation of option A and its risk list, sent just after his 04:26Z question. The thread's decision card (options A / B) is closed on A.

Ruling-ref: this comment.

What this carries:
- PR #35261 implements A. It also closes a gap the risk review found: an environment-saved capability is not excused at the `everyone` anchor. Only a declaration with package provenance is (ADR-0090 D5).
- ADR-0126 §9 lists "reopening any code-only type (field, job, api, capability, agent)" as not chartered. The amendment note recording this ruling goes in a separate governed PR.
- Item 2 (scaffold plugins): the scaffold stops writing connector plugins; the install contract is unchanged.

Discussed in the same thread and **not ruled**: keeping a template's own namespace by default (cloud#3648's customer-code prefix) and reserving official prefixes (ADR-0048 addendum A.2/A.4). No card has been filed for it.

Stamped 2026-11-19T04:32Z.

coordinator#1 · os-warren · session_01JQwxbXuXMUwP5Bbmq6UZRJ

**Ruled: the `everyone`-anchor bound stands as it is** — the follow-up question from the contract review on PR #35261 (record 7000301544, S2).

Maintainer, in the project thread at 2026-11-19T05:27Z, tapping option 「接受现有边界」 on the card 「确认管理员可在自己的应用里声明权限点并开放给全员吗」. That option reads: 「平台权限和别的应用已声明的权限点照旧一律挡住；只有没人声明过的名字，管理员能在可编辑的应用里声明一次。本次只把说明写准。」

Ruling-ref: this comment.

What this carries, and a correction to record 6999763503:
- Record 6999763503 said PR #35261 "closes a gap: an environment-saved capability is not excused at the `everyone` anchor". That holds for a capability saved with no package only. A declaration saved into a writable package (a copy, a duplicate, a base the environment authors) carries that package's id and is excused, because a row cannot tell a copied declaration from one saved by hand into the same package.
- The bound that holds: a platform capability's name and a name a package already declares are refused at the save door, and the platform floor applies again at the anchor. A name nobody declares can be declared once, by a `manage_metadata` holder, inside a writable package; that declaration decides its `scope` and excuses it at the anchor.
- No stricter refusal is built. PR #35261's comment, changeset and docs page state this bound; the metadata-service fallback gets the same provenance test.
